implementation: e2e/compose.json has explicit immutable images, separate migrate/setup services, named per-instance database/adapter volumes and an internal-only bridge. No published ports, production inputs, automatic migration or external SMTP/catalog source.

e2e/environment.py plus scripts/e2e-environment.py expose provision/wait/restart/capture/cleanup. New UUID directory only, exclusive lock, private snapshot/file credentials, immutable-input qualification, exact project/owner/resource/PID guards, bounded failures and truthful ready handoff. Cleanup captures before exact scoped down/removal and verifies port/secret/resource cleanup.

e2e/relay.py inherits exactly two already-bound loopback public/source sockets. It forwards opaque TCP only to private public/source 8080, with bounded connections/threads and no payload logging, Docker API, arbitrary proxy destination or extra administration endpoint. Wait refreshes live targets after observed same-container bridge-IP changes.

tests/test_e2e_environment.py has 13 configuration/ownership/lock/failure/redaction/real-relay regressions under approved tests/**. scripts/check-e2e-environment.py exercises real images, PostgreSQL/HTTP/SMTP, all retained restart modes, installed provider bytes, runtime/source failures, lower-layer migration/startup failures, external network/DNS isolation, Docker29 publication behavior and exact cleanup/foreign-target refusal.

diagnostics: Initial Compose qualification stopped before resource creation because Docker's missing-volume response is lowercase 'no such volume'; inspection had recognized only 'No such'. The case-insensitive absence check preserves failure on daemon/permission errors, adds a focused regression, and the initial instance was safely cleaned with retained output.

Second/third qualifications retained/restored all services correctly, then hit harness assumptions: private adapter rejects missing auth with documented 403, not 401; a cached adapter bridge IP could point at the backend after Docker stop/start reassignment. Tests now refresh actual private addresses. Controller wait additionally refreshes an alive relay's target addresses, proven by deliberate reverse-allocation-order restarts with unchanged container IDs.

Fourth qualification passed retained recovery, independent outages, all private endpoint and egress/publication checks, and actual migration refusal; only its expected error string mismatched the existing safe 'Migration failed; no destructive fallback attempted' output. Correcting that oracle completes the real migration/startup/failure/cleanup suite without changing product behavior or weakening validation.

All failed development outputs remain diagnostic exit 1, not passing checks. Two later complete lifecycle outputs exit 0; the final output anchors current controller/topology/relay hashes and the added 144-file relay/context checks. No orchestration/driver or permission-profile repair was made.
